If we have -d + 0.25*r, this could be interpreted as: we want to balance the distance to the candidate (minimize d, hence -d) with the idea of NOT closing the tour too early. A candidate far from start might be a good intermediate step. Actually, in TSP construction, you often want to visit far cities while you have the chance, because if you visit them last, return_distance dominates.

Actually yes! That's the intuition: visit cities that are FAR from start EARLY so that the return trip at the end is short. So -d + alpha*r with alpha > 0 means: minimize distance to candidate, but if candidate is far from start, give it higher priority (to visit it before it's too late). This makes sense!

OK so parent's logic: early on (p small), r weight is low (0.15) - mostly just minimize distance. Late (p large), r weight is high (0.55) - prefer candidates far from start to ensure they get visited before the end.

And regret: positive regret means second_nearest > nearest, so the candidate has a clear "nearest" neighbor among remaining cities. High regret = candidate is close to one specific other city. Low regret = candidate is equidistant to many. The parent adds positive regret weight, so prefers HIGH regret candidates, meaning candidates that have a clear next step. Early in tour this matters more (avoid dead-ends).
